title: GTA6 and Scrapped Liberty City DLC Revealed in Massive 200GB GTA5 Leak
description: GTA6 Hub coverage: A massive 200GB GTA 5 leak suggests Rockstar Games scrapped a Liberty City DLC and includes very early GTA 6 files (unconfirmed rumor).
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Massive 200GB Leak Shakes the Community

According to a recent report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, a massive leak involving nearly 200GB of source code and files related to Grand Theft Auto V has surfaced online. This substantial data breach has once again turned the spotlight onto Rockstar Games, offering a rare and unfiltered look into the developer's historical development pipeline over the past decade. Among the uncovered materials are strong indications of a previously planned, yet ultimately scrapped, single-player expansion, alongside very early traces of work related to the highly anticipated GTA 6.

## The Scrapped Liberty City DLC Plans

One of the most intriguing discoveries within this massive 200GB leak points to plans for a major Liberty City DLC for GTA 5. For years, fans have speculated about whether Rockstar would bring back the iconic setting of GTA 4 into the newer engine. The leaked source code and related files suggest that the studio did indeed begin preliminary work on expanding the game's world to include Liberty City. However, as the unprecedented and sustained financial success of GTA Online took center stage, Rockstar ultimately shifted its priorities, leading to the cancellation of these single-player expansion plans.

## Early Glimpses of GTA 6 Development

In addition to the shelved single-player content for GTA 5, the leaked repository reportedly contains extremely early files and assets tied to the development of GTA 6. It is important to emphasize that because these files stem from the earliest phases of conceptualization and prototyping, they do not represent a playable state or a final vision of the upcoming title. Instead, they serve as a historical footprint, illustrating how Rockstar quietly laid the groundwork for their next-generation open-world masterpiece behind closed doors while wrapping up their previous projects.

## Editor's Take

This 200GB leak (unconfirmed rumor) offers a bittersweet look at what could have been. While the cancellation of a Liberty City DLC is undoubtedly disappointing for single-player enthusiasts, it ultimately paved the way for the era of GTA Online. As we look forward to the official rollout of GTA 6, these unearthed relics from the cutting-room floor simply remind us of the complex, unpredictable nature of AAA game development.
